blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team registers a MIP_SOLUTION callback that appends each solution's value to a list, and solves a 300-variable MIP with HiGHS through MathOpt 9.15. The solve ends OPTIMAL and the list is empty. Why?

options.text: The callback must return terminate=False to be called again
options.says: terminate defaults to False; it only stops a solve, and the callback was never called a first time.

options.text: HiGHS accepts the registration but does not call the callback
options.says: Right: in the runner HiGHS accepted every event and called none, with no error.

options.text: HiGHS found the optimum at the root, so no solution event happened
options.says: Any solve that ends OPTIMAL found at least one feasible solution; SCIP and CP-SAT reported theirs on the same model.

options.text: MIP_SOLUTION is reserved for Gurobi, as PRESOLVE and SIMPLEX are
options.says: SCIP and CP-SAT both called a MIP_SOLUTION callback in lesson 4.3.5; only PRESOLVE, SIMPLEX and BARRIER are Gurobi-only.

origin.section: A Solve Callback Runs at Events the Solver Supports

questions.stem: A crew rule is left out of a model and added by a MIP_SOLUTION callback with add_lazy_constraints=True. On HiGHS in MathOpt 9.15 the solve ends OPTIMAL. What does the team know about the plan?

options.text: It meets the crew rule, since an OPTIMAL plan meets every rule
options.says: OPTIMAL covers the rows the solver saw; HiGHS never saw the lazy ones and returned a plan that broke the rule.

options.text: It meets the crew rule, since HiGHS added the lazy rows at the end
options.says: HiGHS never called the callback, so no lazy row was ever added ('rows sent 0').

options.text: The solve was refused, since HiGHS rejects lazy constraints
options.says: CP-SAT refuses them; HiGHS accepts the registration and goes on without them.

options.text: Nothing about the crew rule until the plan is checked against it
options.says: Right: HiGHS never called the callback, so the rule was never applied; only a check of the plan in Python tells, as starts_per_year did.

origin.section: A Lazy Constraint Is Added Only When a Solution Breaks It

questions.stem: A scenario fixes project P9's start to 2028 and caps the 2029 budget. The deletion filter returns budget_2029 (upper side) and must_P4 (lower side), and no variable bounds. What does that say about P9's fixed start?

options.text: It causes the conflict, since it is the scenario's own change
options.says: Every bound in an IIS is needed for the conflict; P9's bound is not in it, so this conflict holds without it.

options.text: It was skipped, since deletion filters test rows only
options.says: The filter tests the bounds of the variables it is given; P9's start was among them, and it was dropped as not needed.

options.text: It is not part of this conflict, which holds without it
options.says: Right: an IIS keeps only what the conflict needs, as with P032's promise in lesson 4.3.5.

options.text: It caused a second conflict, since an IIS lists one rule per conflict
options.says: An IIS lists every rule one conflict needs, here two rows; it says nothing of other conflicts.

origin.section: A Deletion Filter Finds One by Hand, in the Same Result Type
